basic_information.name: LlamaIndex
basic_information.creator: LlamaIndex Inc. (founded by Jerry Liu, previously a researcher/engineer at Apple, Quora, Two Sigma, and Uber)
basic_information.description: LlamaIndex is the leading open-source data framework for building LLM-powered applications over custom data. Originally launched as 'GPT Index' in November 2022, it provides a comprehensive pipeline for data ingestion, parsing, indexing, retrieval, and response synthesis. With over 300 integration packages, 160+ data connectors via LlamaHub, and support for all major LLM providers, LlamaIndex is particularly strong for RAG workflows, knowledge assistants, and agentic document processing. Its commercial arm, LlamaCloud, offers managed parsing (LlamaParse), indexing, and one-click agent deployment, making it a full-spectrum solution from prototype to production.
basic_information.release_date: November 2022 (initial release as GPT Index); v0.14.13 released January 2026 (latest major version as of Feb 2026)

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Library (open-source Python/TypeScript SDK) + managed cloud API (LlamaCloud). The open-source core is a modular framework with swappable components for ingestion, indexing, retrieval, post-processing, and response synthesis. LlamaCloud adds a serverless managed layer for parsing, indexing, classification, and agent deployment.
technical_architecture.language: Python (primary), TypeScript (LlamaIndex.TS for server-side JS/TS applications)
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports any embedding dimension — integrates with all major embedding providers (OpenAI text-embedding-3 up to 3072d, Cohere Embed v3/v4, Google Gemini, Voyage AI, open-source models via HuggingFace/Ollama). No hard limit on dimensions.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: LlamaIndex itself is not a vector database but an orchestration layer that delegates indexing to underlying vector stores. Supports HNSW (via Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Chroma, Milvus), IVF (via FAISS, Milvus), flat/brute-force (in-memory SimpleVectorStore), DiskANN (via specialized backends), and product/binary quantization through supported vector stores. Also supports keyword indexes (BM25), knowledge graph indexes (Neo4j, Nebula), tree/list indexes for hierarchical retrieval, and SQL-based structured indexes.
technical_architecture.scalability: Scales with the underlying infrastructure choice. In-memory SimpleVectorStore for prototyping; persistent vector stores (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, pgvector, etc.) for millions to billions of vectors. LlamaCloud provides managed horizontal scaling. Multi-tenancy supported through metadata filtering and per-user index partitioning. No inherent vector count limit — constrained only by chosen backend.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Self-hosted (pip install, Docker, Kubernetes), LlamaCloud managed service, cloud-agnostic (works on AWS, GCP, Azure). LlamaCloud provides serverless managed parsing and indexing. LlamaAgents enables one-click deployment of document processing agents. Also integrates with Google Cloud Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, and Databricks.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector retrieval (semantic similarity), sparse retrieval (BM25 keyword search), hybrid search (combining dense + sparse with configurable fusion), knowledge graph retrieval (via Neo4j, Nebula Graph property graph abstractions), SQL/structured data retrieval, multi-vector retrieval, recursive retrieval (parent-child document relationships), auto-retrieval with metadata filters, LLM-based retrieval (LLM selects relevant documents), agentic retrieval (agent decides retrieval strategy dynamically).
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Fixed-size chunking (default 1024 tokens, 20 token overlap), sentence-based splitting, semantic chunking (SemanticSplitterNodeParser analyzing consecutive sentence similarity), recursive character splitting, token-based splitting, document-structure-aware parsing (via LlamaParse for headings, tables, layouts), hierarchical node parsing (parent/child relationships for recursive retrieval). Recommended ranges: 400-800 tokens for prose, 80-160 for code.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in LLMRerank (uses LLM to score and reorder retrieved nodes), cross-encoder reranking (via Cohere Rerank, BGE Reranker integrations), ColBERT-based reranking (via RAGatouille integration), MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) for diversity, score fusion for hybrid search results. Reranking is a first-class node post-processor in the pipeline.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Full multimodal RAG pipeline support: separate vector stores for text and images, multimodal LLM synthesis (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini). LlamaParse supports 90+ file types including embedded images, complex layouts, multi-page tables, handwritten notes. Multimodal mode uses vision models for document parsing. Audio and video embedding support through third-party integrations.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: Native knowledge graph index for entity/relationship extraction from text. GraphRAG v2 pipeline using LlamaIndex PropertyGraph abstractions with Neo4j. Integration with Cognee for advanced GraphRAG workflows. Knowledge Graph RAG Query Engine for graph-enhanced retrieval. Supports building knowledge graphs from unstructured text and querying them alongside vector retrieval.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Built-in CitationQueryEngine that tracks source attributions, returning responses with inline citations pointing to specific source chunks. Supports grounding verification by showing which text segments informed the answer. Enables 'groundedness' scoring to measure response fidelity to retrieved sources.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Response synthesis modes handle context window limits: 'refine' mode iteratively processes chunks, 'tree_summarize' hierarchically condenses information, 'compact' mode packs maximum context per LLM call. Supports context compression via LLM summarization. Retrieval-stage filtering (metadata, reranking, top-k selection) ensures only the most relevant content reaches the LLM. Sub-question query engine decomposes complex queries to fit within context limits.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Framework overhead approximately 6ms (measured in comparative benchmarks vs LangChain's ~10ms). End-to-end query latency depends heavily on chosen LLM, embedding model, and vector store. Typical RAG query with OpenAI GPT-4 + Pinecone: 1-3 seconds total. Cold-start latency on first query after restart can be higher — pre-warming indexes recommended for production.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Depends on underlying infrastructure. LlamaParse processes documents asynchronously in batch. LlamaCloud managed service handles concurrent requests with auto-scaling. Open-source library throughput limited by chosen vector store and LLM API rate limits. Token usage is notably efficient: ~1,600 tokens per query vs LangChain's ~2,400 tokens in comparative tests.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: LlamaIndex reported 35% boost in retrieval accuracy in 2025 improvements. LlamaParse claims 90%+ pass-through rates with agentic workflows for document processing. Accuracy depends heavily on chunking strategy, embedding model, and reranking configuration. Framework provides built-in evaluation modules for faithfulness, relevance, and correctness metrics.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: No standardized framework-level benchmark (LlamaIndex is an orchestrator, not a model). Performance varies by configuration. In head-to-head comparisons with LangChain, LlamaIndex shows lower token usage (~1.6k vs ~2.4k) and lower framework overhead (~6ms vs ~10ms). Retrieval quality benchmarks depend on chosen embedding model and vector store. LlamaIndex provides evaluation tools (faithfulness, relevance evaluators) for self-benchmarking. [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: LlamaIndex IS a primary orchestration framework (along with LangChain). Integrates with: LangChain (bidirectional — can use LangChain tools/agents within LlamaIndex and vice versa), DSPy (for prompt optimization), Haystack (limited integration). Over 300 integration packages. Many recommend using LlamaIndex for ingestion/indexing alongside LangChain/LangGraph for orchestration.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: All major LLM providers: OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-4o, o1, o3, GPT-5), Anthropic (Claude 3.5/4 family including Opus 4.1), Google (Gemini 1.5/2.0), Mistral AI, DeepSeek, Cohere, Perplexity, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face (local models via Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp). Day-zero support for new model releases. Unified LLM interface allowing hot-swapping providers.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Yes — native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support. LlamaIndex agents can connect to any MCP-compatible server in one line of code. MCP server available for documentation search. Agent Workflows support ACP integration (filesystem tools, MCP servers, persistent memory). Active MCP development throughout 2025.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: 160+ data connectors via LlamaHub: Google Drive, Notion, Slack, Confluence, SharePoint, S3, GCS, databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB), web crawlers, GitHub repos, Jira, Salesforce, HubSpot, email (Gmail, Outlook), PDF, DOCX, PPTX, CSV, JSON, and more. Each connector handles authentication, pagination, and incremental updates. LlamaCloud adds managed connectors with scheduling.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Built-in observability via OpenTelemetry and Jaeger tracing for step-by-step pipeline monitoring. Compatible with Arize Phoenix, Langfuse, LangSmith, Braintrust, and other LLMOps platforms. Workflow Debugger for visual workflow inspection, real-time event logs, and run comparison. Instrumentation module for custom callback handlers and span tracking.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core model. The open-source framework (llama-index) is free under MIT license. LlamaCloud (managed service) uses credit-based pricing: 1,000 credits = $1.25. Plans: Free (10k credits/month), Starter, Pro, and Enterprise tiers with increasing credit allotments and features. Pay-as-you-go for additional credits at $0.001 per credit.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Open-source framework: completely free, unlimited use. LlamaCloud Free tier: 10,000 credits per month (enough for initial prototyping and testing). LlamaParse free usage included for basic document parsing.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: LlamaParse Premium: $45 per 1,000 pages (reduced from $75). LlamaCloud credits: $0.00125 per credit ($1.25 per 1,000 credits). Enterprise pricing is custom. For self-hosted open-source deployments, costs are infrastructure only (compute + vector store + LLM API costs). At scale, the primary costs are LLM API calls and vector store hosting, not the framework itself.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: For self-hosted: framework cost is zero (MIT license). Main costs: embedding API ($0.02-0.13 per 1M tokens for OpenAI), LLM API ($2.50-75 per 1M tokens depending on model), vector store ($0-25+/month for managed Pinecone, free for local Chroma/pgvector), compute infrastructure ($50-500+/month depending on scale). For LlamaCloud managed: monthly subscription + per-credit usage. LlamaParse adds $45/1K pages for premium parsing. Total POC cost: <$50/month; production enterprise: $500-5,000+/month depending on volume.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the RAG framework market, alongside LangChain. LlamaIndex is considered the go-to framework specifically optimized for data retrieval and RAG, while LangChain is broader in scope. LlamaIndex has grown to 3M+ monthly downloads, 46,900+ GitHub stars, and a waitlist of 10,000+ organizations including 90 Fortune 500 companies. Positioned as the 'batteries-included' RAG framework vs LangChain's more general-purpose orchestration approach.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Salesforce, KPMG (minority equity investor), Carlyle Group (private equity), Rakuten, Cemex (global building materials), Jeppesen/Boeing (saves ~2,000 engineering hours), Databricks (strategic investor). 90 Fortune 500 companies on LlamaCloud waitlist. Used broadly across financial services, consulting, manufacturing, and technology sectors.
adoption_and_market.community_size: GitHub: ~46,900 stars, 6,800 forks (run-llama/llama_index). PyPI: 3M+ monthly downloads across packages (llama-index-readers-llama-parse alone: 6.7M monthly downloads). LinkedIn: 230,000+ followers. Active Discord community. 1,600+ contributors on GitHub. Over 300 integration packages maintained by community and core team.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: $27.5M over 3 rounds. Series A: $19M (March 2025), led by Norwest Venture Partners, participation from Greylock. Additional strategic investments from Databricks and KPMG (May 2025). Pre-money valuation at Series A: ~$93M. Seed/earlier rounds backed by Greylock. 9 investors total.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Primary competitor: LangChain (broader orchestration, larger community ~100K stars). Other competitors: Haystack (by deepset, more opinionated pipeline design), DSPy (Stanford, programmatic prompt optimization), Semantic Kernel (Microsoft, .NET-focused), Vectara (managed RAG-as-a-service), Unstructured (document processing focused). LlamaIndex differentiators: best-in-class document parsing (LlamaParse), deep RAG specialization, modular index abstractions, lower framework overhead and token usage, integrated managed service (LlamaCloud).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for startups building document-heavy AI products (legal tech, fintech, healthcare, compliance, knowledge management). Best fit: teams of 1-10 engineers who need production RAG without building from scratch. Budget-friendly: open-source core is free, LlamaCloud has accessible free tier for prototyping. Use case fit: internal knowledge assistants, customer support bots, document processing automation, contract review, due diligence tools. Not ideal for: teams needing only simple chatbots (overkill), or teams requiring extreme low-latency real-time systems where framework overhead matters.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Start with open-source LlamaIndex for POC (free, full control, learn the abstractions). Move to LlamaCloud when: (1) document parsing quality matters (LlamaParse handles complex layouts that open-source parsers miss), (2) team wants to avoid managing indexing infrastructure, (3) need one-click agent deployment. Self-host when: strict data residency requirements, cost-sensitive at high volume, need deep customization. Use LlamaCloud when: speed-to-market matters more than infrastructure control, team is small, or document processing is core to the product.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC/demo: 1-2 days (VectorStoreIndex + query engine in <50 lines of code). MVP with basic RAG: 1-2 weeks (add persistent vector store, better chunking, reranking). Production-ready with evaluation: 4-8 weeks (add observability, CI/CD, evaluation pipeline, error handling, caching). Enterprise deployment with LlamaCloud: 2-4 weeks (managed infrastructure accelerates timeline). LlamaAgents Builder can produce extraction workflows in minutes for supported use cases.
key_lessons: Start simple with VectorStoreIndex and default settings, then layer in complexity (better parsing, hybrid retrieval, reranking) based on measured evaluation metrics — premature optimization wastes weeks.
Document parsing quality is the single biggest lever for RAG accuracy — investing in LlamaParse or careful preprocessing pays off more than tuning retrieval algorithms.
Use LlamaIndex's built-in evaluation tools (faithfulness, relevance) from day one to establish baselines — without metrics, you cannot systematically improve your RAG pipeline.

The combination of LlamaIndex for ingestion/indexing and LangGraph for complex orchestration is increasingly the recommended production pattern — use each framework for its strength rather than forcing one to do everything.
Plan for multimodal from the start if your documents contain tables, charts, or images — retrofitting multimodal RAG is significantly harder than designing for it upfront.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes — LlamaCloud provides: (1) Index no-code UI for creating, managing, and testing indexes and data pipelines, (2) LlamaAgents Builder (beta) for natural language workflow creation, (3) LlamaIndex Classify for rules-based document classification with templates. However, the no-code interfaces focus on document processing and indexing — full application building still requires code.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools — LlamaCloud no-code interfaces), Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — RAG architecture decisions, Build vs Buy with LlamaCloud), Session 4 (AI business models — credit-based pricing, open-core model, $93M valuation case study)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official LlamaIndex documentation, GitHub API, PR Newswire press releases, TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE, KPMG official announcements, Google Cloud blog, and multiple independent technical reviews. Pricing and feature data verified against official LlamaIndex developer documentation.
confidence.cross_reference: Funding confirmed by PR Newswire, TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE, KPMG, and Tracxn. GitHub stars verified via GitHub API (46,892 as of Feb 2026). Enterprise customers confirmed by company blog, KPMG press release, and TechCrunch reporting. confidence.caveats: LlamaIndex is evolving rapidly — features like LlamaAgents Builder are in beta and may change. Pricing credits and plan structures may be updated. The 35% retrieval accuracy improvement claim comes from a comparison source rather than a peer-reviewed benchmark. Valuation ($93M) is pre-money from March 2025 Series A — current valuation may differ. Framework overhead benchmarks (6ms vs 10ms) are from a single comparative study and may vary by configuration. LlamaCloud waitlist numbers (10,000+ orgs, 90 Fortune 500) are self-reported.
confidence.security_posture: Known vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-1793 (critical SQL injection in LlamaIndex, patched). General RAG attack surfaces apply: knowledge base poisoning (compromised vector stores can inject misinformation), prompt injection through retrieved content, embedding inversion attacks. LlamaIndex does not provide built-in prompt injection detection — teams must implement input validation, output filtering, and privilege limitations. LlamaCloud inherits standard cloud security (encryption at rest/in transit, SOC 2 compliance in progress). Best practices: use verified datasets, implement provenance tracking, monitor model drift, run adversarial testing, design for containment with limited AI privileges.
